description: A/B for bucket-aligned step packing. Run once per server mode against the SAME build, with BUCKETLADDER_ALIGN deciding which. Correctness is gated first: greedy completions at prompt lengths chosen to straddle compiled buckets, hashed and compared across modes. If the hashes differ the patch is wrong and no timing here means anything.
note_prompt_lens: 520, 1032 and 2056 sit just above 512, 1024 and 2048 -- exactly the steps the patch trims. 128 is a control that never triggers it. If the patch corrupts anything it will be at these lengths.
note_output_len: 16, not 1. The patch defers PREFILL chunks, so a workload with real decode is the one where deferral could plausibly disturb output, and decode is also where production serving spends its time.
note_both_sides: Throughput and p99 are both recorded. The optimisation defers work, so a throughput number without the tail-latency cost would be exactly the one-sided report the plan warned about.
